name: application-follow-button
title: Follow Button
description: Stateful follow button: "Follow" when not following, "Following" that swaps to a red "Unfollow" on hover/focus, and a disabled "Requested" state for pending follow requests.
useWhen: Building a social feature where users can follow/unfollow another user or page.
The target account may be private, requiring a pending "Requested" state distinct from an active follow.
Pairing with Person Hovercard or a profile page header as the primary relationship action.
avoidWhen: The action is a simple binary favorite/save with no social-relationship semantics — use Wishlist Heart Toggle instead.
You need to follow multiple items in a compact list (e.g. a search results row) where the full-width hover-to-unfollow treatment is too heavy — a smaller icon-only toggle may fit better.
responsiveBehavior: The button has a fixed minimum width in its following/requested states so the label swap on hover doesn't shift surrounding layout.
accessibility: The hover-to-unfollow swap also responds to focus (not just mouse hover), so keyboard users see the same "Unfollow" affordance before activating it.
The requested state uses a real disabled button, removing it from the tab order rather than faking a disabled look on an active control.
Each state's meaning is carried by its visible label text ("Follow", "Following", "Unfollow", "Requested"), not color alone.

variants.title: Follow Button
variants.description: Four states stacked: not-followed (indigo Follow), Following at rest, Following's red Unfollow hover state, and a disabled Requested state.
accessibility: The Unfollow hover state is also reachable via keyboard focus, not mouse-only.

variants.title: Follow Button (Dark)
variants.description: The same four states adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Button borders and the red hover-state contrast remain distinguishable against the dark surface.
